newsitem.title: LATVIA: O/N RATES SEEN EASING, DOLLAR UP VS LAT.
newsitem.headline: O/N RATES SEEN EASING, DOLLAR UP VS LAT.

text.p: Overnight rates were seen easing in Latvia as banks fulfilled their reserve requirements and the lat lost ground against the surging dollar, dealers said on Tuesday.
Overnight rates were in a bid/ask range of 4.00/5.00 percent and were expected to fall.
"Banks are meeting their reserve requirements and so overnight rates should fall this week," said Maris Vinklers, head of money markets at Hansabank-Latvija.
He added that there was growing demand for one to two-month loans on the market, driven by foreign players ahead of the privatisation of key state assets.
Dealers said the need for lats to participate in privatisation could lead to a big demand for lats over the next few weeks.
Russia's Gazprom, which was awarded a big stake in Latvian Gas earlier this year, is also expected to come to the market soon to pay for its shares in the Latvian gas distributor.
The lat sagged against the dollar on Tuesday as the U.S. currency soared to a fresh 71-month high against the mark.
The interbank lat/dollar rate was 0.5772/77 late on Tuesday morning, near the Latvian central bank's intervention rate of 0.5772/888.
